expectations.text: Covers the GDPR Art. 28(3) mandatory clause set: documented instructions, confidentiality, security measures, sub-processor rules, data subject rights assistance, breach notification, deletion/return at end, audit rights
expectations.evidence: Lists documented instructions, confidentiality, Art. 32 security, sub-processor conditions, DSAR assistance, Art. 33-36 breach assistance, "Return or deletion of personal data at the end", and audit rights

expectations.text: Explains sub-processor authorisation mechanics (Art. 28(2)): specific or general written authorisation with change notification and objection opportunity, plus equivalent flow-down (Art. 28(4)) and processor liability
expectations.evidence: Covers "specific prior authorization or general authorization with notice and the right to object" and flow-down, but omits processor liability under Art. 28(4)

expectations.text: Reviews the sub-processor list for fourth-party concentration, transfer destinations/mechanisms, and change-notification lead time
expectations.evidence: Checks locations/transfer mechanisms and "30 days' notice with a right to object", but never assesses fourth-party concentration risk

expectations.text: States that US employee health data for a benefits program raises HIPAA business associate questions: a DPA is not a BAA — 45 CFR 164.308(b)/164.314(a) assurances are separate
expectations.evidence: "you likely need a separate Business Associate Agreement (BAA)... get a BAA executed in addition to, not instead of, the standard DPA" — DPA is not a BAA, separate HIPAA assurances required

expectations.text: Produces an actionable clause-by-clause output (present/absent/deficient or checklist form) rather than generic prose
expectations.evidence: Actionable checklist form: itemised clause list plus "Confirm... Check... Verify... Flag..." action bullets for the sub-processor review, not generic prose
